# Negative integer flux for an actual balanced pair of active caps

We use ambient coordinates `(z,x,y)` in `R x R^2` and ordinary
mixed-integer area. All measures and fluxes in the main calculation are
unnormalized. The example has maximum depth exactly `1/2`; it is not a
counterexample to any proposed lower bound below `1/2`.

## 1. The exact convex body and its fibers

Let

`K=conv{(-1,-1),(9/4,0),(-1,1)}`,
`B=(K-K)/2`,
`C=conv( {-1} x (-K), {1} x K )`.

The middle set `{0} x B` can equivalently be included in this convex hull.
Indeed, for every `t in [-1,1]`, the exact fiber is

`C_t=((1-t)/2)(-K)+((1+t)/2)K`.                       (1)

To prove (1), every convex combination of the two endpoint layers has the
specified total weights by its first coordinate. Convexity of each
endpoint fiber combines all its individual points into one point of that
fiber. Conversely every indicated Minkowski combination is in the convex
hull. In particular the induced mixed-integer set has exactly three
nonempty fibers:

`S_{-1}=-K`, `S_0=B`, `S_1=K`.

The body `C` is compact, convex, and full dimensional: it contains a
two-dimensional body in its middle plane and points on both sides of
that plane. It is centrally symmetric under `(z,x,y)->(-z,-x,-y)`.
The same is true of `S`, and `0 in S`.

The six vertices of `B`, in counterclockwise order, are

`(-13/8,-1/2), (0,-1), (13/8,-1/2),`
`(13/8,1/2), (0,1), (-13/8,1/2)`.

They are the extreme pairwise half-differences of the three vertices of
`K`; taking their convex hull gives the whole difference body. Its area
can also be read as a rectangle of width `13/4` and height `1`, plus two
triangles of base `13/4` and height `1/2`. Thus

`w:=|K|=13/4`, `|B|=39/8`, `M:=H_2(S)=2w+|B|=91/8`.    (2)

The centroid of `K` is `(1/12,0)`, by averaging its three vertices. The
centroids of `-K` and `B` are `(-1/12,0)` and `(0,0)`. All three fibers
have positive area, so the intrinsic dimension in the task is `q=2`,
and `H_2(S)` is exactly the sum in (2), with standard Hausdorff
normalization.

## 2. Exact global depth and an active balanced cap pair

Let

`H_+={x>=0}`, `H_-={x<=0}`.

For every closed ambient halfspace `H` containing the origin, central
symmetry gives `H_2(S intersect H)>=M/2`: the two reflected halfspaces
`H` and `-H` cover the whole ambient space, and their intersections with
`S` have equal measure. This argument includes vertical halfspaces and
halfspaces carrying positive boundary mass.

The boundaries of `H_+` and `H_-` have zero two-dimensional measure in
each fiber, so each of these caps has mass exactly `M/2=91/16`.
Consequently the depth of the origin is exactly `1/2` and both caps are
active. The maximum depth is also exactly `1/2`: for any point of `S`,
the two opposite halfspaces through it with fixed continuous normal
`(1,0)` have masses adding to `M`, since the scalar `x`-law has no atoms.
At least one of their masses is at most `M/2`.

Their full ambient inward normals are

`a_+=(0,1,0)`, `a_-=(0,-1,0)`.

The positive weights `1/2,1/2` balance these normals exactly. More strongly,
every nonvertical halfspace through the origin has mass `M/2`, since its
boundary cuts each continuous fiber in a set of area zero and reflection
exchanges its strict sides. Thus the two specified caps are actual global
minimizers over the full ambient normal family, rather than merely over
fiber-parallel directions.

## 3. Sections and coarea gradients

At `x=0`, the section of each endpoint fiber is the interval
`-9/13<=y<=9/13`, of length `18/13`. The section of `B` is
`-1<=y<=1`, of length `2`. The mixed section mass, with the continuous
normal of length one, is therefore

`L=18/13+2+18/13=62/13`.                              (3)

Each interval has `y`-centroid zero. The two endpoint intervals have
equal length at opposite indices, and every section point has `x=0`.
Consequently the full ambient section centroid is exactly `(0,0,0)`:

`sum_z z S_z=0`, `sum_z integral_(section_z) (x,y)dy=(0,0)`.

In particular the first variation of the cap mass with respect to any
normal perturbation fixing the origin is zero. Explicitly, at `H_+`,
for a variation of the affine functional
`v z+u_x x+u_y y-t`, coarea gives

`delta mass = delta v sum_z z S_z
             + delta u_x sum_z integral x
             + delta u_y sum_z integral y - delta t L
           = -delta t L`.

All cuts here are proper; the middle cutting line passes through two
vertices, which does not create boundary area or invalidate this first
variation. Central symmetry also proves the zero normal derivatives
directly. The opposite cap has the same section mass. For translations
of the cap center, the two gradients are `-L a_+` and `-L a_-`, and their
equal-weight sum is zero. Thus the active pair satisfies both normal
balance and coarea-gradient balance.

## 4. Exact flux and its sign

For an oriented scalar functional `ell`, let `m_z` be its mean on fiber
`z`, let `m` be its mean on all of `S`, and let

`P_z(t)=|S_z intersect {ell>=t}|/|S_z|`.

The integer flux convention is

`J(t)=sum_z |S_z|(m_z-m)P_z(t)`.                       (4)

This is the tree-independent flux in
`candidate 3121a9d11f167d7d`.

For `H_+`, take `ell=x`, `t=0`. The global scalar mean is `m=0`, and
the three fiber means at indices `-1,0,1` are `-1/12,0,1/12`.
The positive cap of `K` is a triangle of height `9/4` and base `18/13`,
so

`|K intersect {x>=0}|=81/52`,
`P_1(0)=81/169`, `P_{-1}(0)=88/169`, `P_0(0)=1/2`.

Substituting in (4) gives exactly

`J_+(0)=(13/4)(1/12)(81/169-88/169)=-7/624<0`.          (5)

For `H_-`, use the oriented functional `ell=-x`. Its fiber means have
the opposite signs and its cap fractions are the complementary ones.
Their two sign changes give

`J_-(0)=-7/624<0`.                                    (6)

Thus the sum of the two active-cap fluxes is `-7/312`, and their
equal-weight average is `-7/624`. Dividing the underlying measure by
`M=91/8` makes each normalized flux exactly

`J_+(0)/M=J_-(0)/M=-1/1014`.

For comparison with a path-flow definition, orient the integer edges
from `-1` to `0` and from `0` to `1`. For `ell=x`, both edge flows are
`13/48`; multiplying them by successive differences of the cap fractions
telescopes to the same value in (5). There is no omitted middle-fiber
mean term: that mean is exactly zero.

## 5. Conditional index and a local flux profile

The obstruction persists even though the derivative correction vanishes
at the central section. For `|t|<=1`, the two endpoint scalar densities
are

`f_1(t)=(18-8t)/13`, `f_{-1}(t)=(18+8t)/13`,

and the middle one is `f_0(t)=2-8|t|/13`. Hence

`f(t)=(62-8|t|)/13`,
`E[z | x=t]=-16t/(62-8|t|)`.

The conditional integer mean has derivative `-8/31` at zero, even
though the unconditional fiber means `m_z=z/12` increase with `z`.

The exact closed tails, again for `|t|<=1`, are

`P_1(t)=(9-4t)^2/169`,
`P_{-1}(t)=1-(9+4t)^2/169`.

Therefore

`J_+(t)=(32t^2-7)/624`,
`R(t):=sum_z(m_z-m)f_z(t)=-4t/39`,
`J_+'(t)=-R(t)`.

In particular `R(0)=0` and the full section centroid is zero, while the
integrated flux is strictly negative. The example refutes a nonnegative
flux assertion even for a balanced pair of actual equal-budget active
caps at a global depth maximizer. It does not refute (OC), and it does
not show failure of a flux inequality under additional hypotheses that
force all other fibers outside a chosen cap.
